reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read Proverbs 1:28 as judgment on those who spurned Wisdom's earlier call, not a limit on Matthew 7:8's promise to sincere seekers.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible sets Matthew 7:8 and Proverbs 8:17's finding-promise directly against Proverbs 1:28's flat denial as an unresolved pairing.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/found.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: Now no prayers or most diligent seeking will avail (Pro 8:17).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB glosses Proverbs 1:28's non-finding by explicitly cross-referencing Proverbs 8:17's finding-promise, naming the two verses as a pair requiring reconciliation.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Then those that slighted God will seek him early (that is, earnestly), but in vain; they shall not find him, because they sought him not when he might be found, Isa 55:6.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Block-anchored note supplies the harmonizing mechanism: the promise to finders presupposes seeking within the window of opportunity, which these seekers had already forfeited.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Because they sought not with an affection to God, but for ease of their own grief.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Offers a second, distinct harmonizing strategy from the same tradition: the non-finding turns on the insincerity of the motive behind the seeking, not on timing alone.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pairing under the heading 'Early seekers successful. Some fail to find,' setting Proverbs 8:17 directly against Proverbs 1:28 and resolving it as addressed to two different classes of seekers -- the diligent young versus obstinate, hardened transgressors (pp. 71-72; verified against the Internet Archive full text).
